title: Sounds in words; holding a pen
cando: hear the sounds in a word, and hold a pen to make lines and circles

about.text: In this lesson you use your ears and a pen. You hear words that end the same and words that start the same. You count the sounds in a word. Then you draw lines and circles, from left to right.
goals: Hear when two words end the same
Hear when two words start the same
Count the sounds in a short word
Hold a pen and make a line and a circle
Write on a line, from left to right

chapters.title: Listening to the sounds in words
chapters.text:
Hello. This is Lesson 1 of Letters & Sounds.
There are no letters in this part. Only your ears.
Reading starts with hearing. Not with letters.
First, words that end the same.
Listen. Man. Pan.
Man. Pan. The end is the same.
We say they rhyme.
Listen again. Pin. Chin. They rhyme.
Now two that do not. Man. Cup.
Man. Cup. Not the same at the end.
Say with me. Man, pan. Rhyme.
Now the start of a word.
Listen. Sun. Sit.
Sun. Sit. The first sound is the same.
Sss. Both start with sss.
Listen. Top. Tap. Both start with t.
Now the hardest part today. Counting.
Every word is made of small sounds.
Listen to the word cat.
C. A. T. Three sounds.
Hold up a finger for each one. C. A. T.
Three fingers. Three sounds.
Now the word up. U. P. Two sounds.
Two fingers. Two sounds.
Do this many times. It gets easier.
When you can hear the sounds, you can read.

chapters.title: Lines and circles
chapters.text:
In this part we use a pen.
You do not need the letter names today.
A letter is a shape. You can copy a shape.
Every letter is made of two things.
Lines and circles. That is all.
Look at l. That is one line.
Look at o. That is one circle.
Look at b. That is a line and a circle.
Now, English is written left to right.
Start on the left. Go to the right.
The letters sit on a line.
Some letters go under the line.
They are g, j, p, q and y.
Now the hard part. Some shapes look the same.
Look at b and d. The circle moves.
In b, the line is first. Then the circle.
In d, the circle is first. Then the line.
Look at p and q. It is the same problem.
Look at m and n. Count the humps.
m has two humps. n has one hump.
Do not hurry. Copy each shape slowly.
A slow letter you can read beats a fast one you cannot.

rhyme.title: Words that rhyme
rhyme.lead: Tap Hear it. Which word ends the same? Tap its picture.

items.spoken: Which one rhymes with man? pan, cup, or sun?
items.why: man, pan: the end is the same.

items.spoken: Which one rhymes with cat? hat, bus, or pen?
items.why: cat, hat: the end is the same.

items.spoken: Which one rhymes with sun? run, bag, or cat?
items.why: sun, run: the end is the same.

items.spoken: Which one rhymes with bell? shell, box, or car?
items.why: bell, shell: the end is the same.

items.spoken: Which one rhymes with car? star, bus, or cup?
items.why: car, star: the end is the same.

start.title: Words that start the same
start.lead: Tap Hear it. Which word starts with the same sound? Tap its picture.

items.spoken: Which one starts like sun? sock, cup, or map?
items.why: sun, sock: both start with sss.

items.spoken: Which one starts like bus? bag, sun, or hat?
items.why: bus, bag: both start with b.

items.spoken: Which one starts like map? milk, pen, or car?
items.why: map, milk: both start with m.

items.spoken: Which one starts like top? tea, box, or fish?
items.why: top, tea: both start with t.

items.spoken: Which one starts like fish? foot, bed, or cat?
items.why: fish, foot: both start with f.

items.spoken: Which one starts like dog? door, sun, or pen?
items.why: dog, door: both start with d.

pen.title: Hold the pen
pen.lead: Listen. Then try it with a real pen and paper.
pen.text:
Hold the pen between your thumb and your first finger.
Let it rest on your middle finger.
Hold it near the point, but not too tight.
Put the paper straight in front of you.
Start on the left. Go to the right.

shapes.title: Lines and circles
shapes.lead: Tap a shape. Trace it with your finger, pen or mouse. Then draw it on paper, from left to right.

count.title: Count the sounds
count.lead: Listen to the word. Hold up a finger for each sound. How many sounds? Tap the number.

items.spoken: uh, puh
kuh, ah, tuh
sss, uh, nnn
eh, guh
buh, uh, sss
sss, tuh, aw, puh
mmm, ih, luh, kuh

listen.title: Start and end
listen.lead: Tap Hear it, then tap the picture.

items.spoken: Which one starts like bus? bed, cup, or sun?
items.why: bus, bed: both start with b.

items.spoken: Which one starts like cat? car, pen, or fish?
items.why: cat, car: both start with k.

items.spoken: Which one rhymes with hat? cat, bus, or egg?
items.why: hat, cat: the end is the same.

items.spoken: Which one starts like man? moon, sock, or door?
items.why: man, moon: both start with m.

copyShapes.title: Copy a row of shapes
copyShapes.lead: Copy each row on paper, from left to right. Or trace it here.

canDo: I can hear when two words rhyme.
I can hear when two words start the same.
I can count the sounds in a short word.
I can hold a pen and draw lines and circles.
